//: A push must not deploy production.
On 9 Sep 2026 a push to `venev-onboarding` produced a production
deployment 60 seconds later, aliased to dashboard.oneeighty.cz. Nobody
asked for it: the branch is Vercel's production branch, so every push to
it shipped the whole app. The team's mental model — and runbook 29 — said
production only moves on `vercel --prod`, and that had been true only
because git builds were silently failing in 4s while `rootDirectory` was
unset. Fixing that setting turned an accident into a deploy pipeline
without anyone deciding to.
`deploymentEnabled: false` stops git-triggered builds for that branch.
It does not touch `vercel --prod`, which is not a git deployment — so
shipping stays a deliberate act, which is what everyone already believed.
AT THE REPOSITORY ROOT, not in dashboard/. The project's root directory
is `dashboard`, so that is where Vercel reads build config from — but the
git gate is evaluated when the webhook arrives, before any root directory
is applied. Placed under dashboard/ it was simply not read: a push on
9 Sep produced a production build with the gate supposedly in force.
The better long-term setting is to point Vercel's production branch at
something nobody pushes and let this branch make previews. That lives in
project settings rather than here; until it is changed, this file is the
gate, and it is in the repo where a reviewer can see it.
